name: P07 — SETTLE: hold one direction 14 s. Does the camera come round behind him, and does it come round SMOOTHLY?

steps.note: S1. The instrument. Two traces of the same walk: the LENS (camera.current/orbit, where the viewer is actually looking) and the BOOM (camera.boom, the ease-behind's own target). If the request is right, these two converge onto the boy's back and stay there.

steps.eval: (async()=>{window.__T=(btn,ms,every)=>new Promise(res=>{const S=[];const t0=performance.now();__DQ.hold(btn);let n=0;const tick=()=>{const st=__DQ.state();const c=st.field.camera;const p=st.player;if(n%every===0)S.push({t:+(performance.now()-t0).toFixed(0),lens:c.current,boom:c.boom,drift:c.drift,hold:c.hold,swing:c.swing,blocked:p.blocked?1:0});n++;if(performance.now()-t0<ms)requestAnimationFrame(tick);else{__DQ.release(btn);res(S);}};requestAnimationFrame(tick);});const D=(a,b)=>Math.abs(((a-b+540)%360)-180);window.__OFF=(s,k)=>s.map(v=>+D(v[k],(360-v.facingX)%360).toFixed(1));return 'ready';})()

steps.note: S2. FACING is fixed on the page too, so the trace can compute 'how far behind is the camera' without a second round trip.

steps.eval: (async()=>{const {Field}=await import('/src/world/field.js');window.__SIMP=()=>{const w=Field.world();return w&&w.player&&w.player.p?w.player.p:null;};__DQ.teleport('meadow',2,8);const w=Field.world();if(w&&w.player&&w.player.face)w.player.face(0);await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,700));window.__T2=(btn,ms,every)=>new Promise(res=>{const S=[];const t0=performance.now();__DQ.hold(btn);let n=0;const tick=()=>{const c=__DQ.state().field.camera;const p=__DQ.state().player;if(n%every===0)S.push({t:+(performance.now()-t0).toFixed(0),lens:c.current,boom:c.boom,drift:c.drift,hold:c.hold,swing:c.swing,blocked:p.blocked?1:0,facingX:p.facing});n++;if(performance.now()-t0<ms)requestAnimationFrame(tick);else{__DQ.release(btn);res(S);}};requestAnimationFrame(tick);});return 'facing captured';})()

steps.note: S3. HOLD ONE DIRECTION 14 SECONDS. This is the request: a player leaning on a direction should see the camera drift round behind him, gently.
S4. THE SHAPE OF IT — 100 ms samples: seconds -> (lens, boom, offByBehind, blocked). blocked 1 means the boy hit a wall and the walk, not the camera, is what stopped.

S5. THE VERDICT NUMBERS. settleS = seconds until offByBehind is under 10 and STAYS under. pathLens = how far the LENS actually travelled in total (a viewer who feels the camera has moved). peakStep = the biggest single-sample jump in the lens, in degrees — this is the wobble.
S6. the same 14 s to the LEFT, mirrored — a fix that only works on one side is not a fix.
